assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.

fresh_terms.name: ~Kab
fresh_terms.purpose: new session key generated by the server for communication between A and B

fresh_terms.name: ~T
fresh_terms.purpose: timestamp/time value inserted by the server for the session-key ticket; explicit clock semantics are not specified

long_term_keys.name: Ksa
long_term_keys.policy: private symmetric setup/state shared by A and S; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

long_term_keys.name: Ksb
long_term_keys.policy: private symmetric setup/state shared by B and S; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: A requests from the server a session key for communication with B by sending the two identities A and B in plaintext.

messages.label: M2
messages.meaning: S generates session key ~Kab and timestamp ~T, then sends B, ~Kab, ~T, and a ticket for B to A encrypted under the long-term A-S key Ksa. The nested ticket is encrypted under Ksb for B.
messages.protection: outer symmetric-encryption under Ksa; nested ticket symmetric-encryption under Ksb

messages.label: M3
messages.meaning: A forwards to B the opaque ticket component received inside M2. The expanded term records the server-created contents, but A does not construct or decrypt this Ksb-encrypted ticket.
messages.protection: symmetric-encryption under Ksb; opaque forwarding by A

checks: select private setup keys Ksa for A-S and Ksb for B-S
parse decrypted outer payload as <B, Kab, T, ticket>
bind Kab to ~Kab and T to ~T from the decrypted payload
carry the ticket component opaquely; A cannot decrypt or verify the Ksb-encrypted ticket contents
parse ticket payload as <Kab, A, T>
bind claimed partner A, session key Kab, and timestamp T from the decrypted ticket
no explicit clock, freshness-window, or replay-cache check for T is specified by the input

checks.condition: receive and parse plaintext request M1 as the ordered pair <A,B>; this does not cryptographically authenticate that the network sender is A
generate a fresh session key Kab for A and B and include the same Kab in both the outer payload for A and the nested ticket for B
include the same timestamp T in both the outer payload for A and the nested ticket for B
decrypt M2 using Ksa and parse ordered fields <B,Kab,T,ticket>; A obtains Kab and T from the outer encryption
treat the nested ticket senc(<Kab,A,T>,Ksb) as opaque and forward the exact received ticket component in M3
decrypt M3 using Ksb and parse ordered fields <Kab,A,T> to obtain the session key, claimed peer A, and timestamp T
timestamp T is available to determine validity, but the input gives no concrete clock or anti-replay validation predicate

events.name: Request_A
events.when: A sends the plaintext request M1 to S

events.name: ServerIssue
events.when: S receives a request naming A and B, generates Kab and timestamp T, and sends M2

events.name: Running_A
events.when: A decrypts M2 under Ksa, obtains Kab and T, and is ready to forward the ticket to B

events.name: A_Forward
events.when: A sends M3 containing the exact opaque ticket extracted from M2

events.name: Commit_B
events.when: B decrypts the ticket M3 with Ksb and accepts Kab, A, and T from the ticket

events.name: B_Accept
events.when: B completes the ticket-processing step and obtains the session key

events.name: Secret
events.when: Emitted by a role that obtains the session key Kab for the A-B session, according to lemma instrumentation

claims.intent: Source/typing lemma for received and decrypted protocol values, including identities A and B, session key Kab, timestamp T, and the forwarded ticket.
event_schema: source facts for M2 decrypted under Ksa as <B,Kab,T,ticket>
source facts for M3 decrypted under Ksb as <Kab,A,T>
claims.witness: Not applicable for all-traces source proof; supplied goal metadata expects verification.

claims.intent: There exists an honest execution trace in which A requests a key for B, S issues the key and ticket, A forwards the ticket, and B accepts.
claims.witness: Honest trace: A -> S: <A,B>; S -> A: senc(<B,Kab,T,senc(<Kab,A,T>,Ksb)>,Ksa); A -> B: senc(<Kab,A,T>,Ksb); B decrypts and accepts.

claims.intent: The session key Kab generated by S for A and B remains secret from the Dolev-Yao adversary in traces without explicit long-term-key or session-key reveal.
event_schema: not K(Kab) unless an explicit reveal/compromise event exposes Kab, Ksa, or Ksb
claims.witness: Not applicable for all-traces secrecy proof; supplied goal metadata expects verification under the no-reveal protocol input.

claims.intent: Whenever B accepts a ticket containing A, Kab, and T, there exists a corresponding non-injective partner/source event, such as A forwarding the ticket and S issuing the ticket for A and B with the same Kab and T.
claims.witness: Not applicable for all-traces authentication proof; replay of the same ticket is still compatible with non-injective agreement because only existence of a matching run is required.

claims.intent: Injective agreement for B is expected to fail because the ticket M3 can be replayed, allowing multiple B acceptances for the same server-issued ticket and A forwarding event.
event_schema: Commit_B(B,A,Kab,T) injectively maps to distinct Running_A(A,B,Kab,T) or A_Forward(A,B,Kab,T,ticket)
claims.witness: Expected counterexample shape: after one honest run creates and forwards ticket senc(<Kab,A,T>,Ksb), the adversary replays the same M3 ticket to B, causing an additional Commit_B with the same Kab and T but without a distinct A forwarding/source event.

compromise.policy: record exact reveal/corruption events, exposed values, and lemma exception timing if the NL/goals mention compromise; this input mentions no explicit reveal or corruption behavior, so secrecy/authentication claims are parsed under no modeled compromise

abstractions: The described network has a single server and multiple agents; this IR instance keeps the named roles A, B, and S from the Alice&Bob notation.
Timestamp T is represented as symbolic server-assigned value ~T; no arithmetic time, expiration window, synchronized clock, or replay cache is added.
No explicit protocol tags are present in the Alice&Bob notation; tuple order and encryption keys provide the parsed structure.
The post-establishment use of Kab for application data is not modeled because it is not described.
M3.term is expanded for auditability, but A's action is opaque forwarding of the ticket from M2, not construction using Ksb.
No reference Sapic+ or Tamarin model is used as a source of protocol behavior; supplied lemma outcomes are retained only as review metadata.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.
The server S is trusted to generate Kab and build both the outer ciphertext and nested ticket consistently.
A and B obtain their long-term server keys Ksa and Ksb from private setup/state.
The Alice&Bob arrows denote intended role flow, not authenticated network channels.
Since the input does not specify a concrete timestamp-validity predicate, B's timestamp handling is recorded as parsing/availability of T rather than a strengthened anti-replay check.
resolved_open_questions: The supplied note says an Alice/Bob notation error from an earlier source was corrected here; this IR uses the corrected three-message notation exactly as provided.
The user-supplied benchmark/reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models are treated as evaluation metadata only and are not used as protocol-behavior sources.

semantic_constraints.policy: M1 is plaintext and unauthenticated; S receives the identities A and B from the network.
S must generate a fresh session key Kab for the response and include the same Kab in the outer ciphertext for A and in the nested ticket for B.
S must include the same timestamp T in the outer ciphertext for A and in the nested ticket for B.
M2 must be encrypted under Ksa so that A can learn B, Kab, T, and the opaque ticket.
The nested ticket in M2 is encrypted under Ksb and is not decryptable by A.
M3 must be the exact ticket component extracted from M2; A does not re-encrypt or modify the ticket contents.
B's evidence for A, Kab, and T comes from decrypting the Ksb-encrypted ticket, not from an authenticated network sender field.
No shared long-term key between A and B may be introduced.
No final key-confirmation message from B to A may be added.
Do not add a stronger freshness, uniqueness, or anti-replay check for T unless a later modeling contract explicitly defines clock semantics.
The adversary may replay any network message, including M3, subject to Dolev-Yao derivability.
